clue.text: Capital has a Thai temple to put back

indicators.note: putting something back here means the whole string of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand

explanation.surface: A city is said to own a temple from Thailand that needs moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put back' reverses the run A WAT TO as a whole, giving the six letters in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada's seat of government is the city named here, so it is a national capital.

clue.text: Choose to remove tail, so climbing a problem for marsupial

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for choose is cut off

parts.note: to choose is to opt

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word so is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Instructions for solving a puzzle about an Australian animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove tail' trims OPT to OP; 'climbing' turns SO into OS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is an American marsupial, carrying its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Sophistication close to worthless in home of the 19 down 23

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Turner Prize is run by and shown at Tate Britain in London

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Refinement nearly worthless where the famous art prize lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The S closing 'worthless' goes inside TATE. 19 down 23 reads TURNER PRIZE, from the answers to those clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Good taste is discernment in aesthetic matters, a kind of refinement or sophistication.

clue.text: See 15
Spooner describes what comes out of the Scottish Parliament as a disease

indicators.note: Spooner's habit of swapping the opening sounds of two words is applied to the phrase that follows

parts.words: what comes out of the Scottish Parliament
parts.note: legislation from Scotland could jokingly be called Jock law; Jock is a slang term for a Scot

parts.words: what comes out of the Scottish Parliament
parts.note: what a parliament produces is law

explanation.surface: A reverend's verbal slip makes Holyrood legislation sound like an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: JOCK LAW with the first letters swapped gives the answer. Jock is British slang, sometimes thought offensive, for a Scottish man.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is commonly called by this name, after the jaw stiffness it causes, so it is a disease.

clue.text: Cover always maintained by sweetheart

indicators.note: being maintained by something is being held within it

parts.note: a sweetheart is a lover
ay is an old or poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A protective layer is kept in place by someone's beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintained by' signals the container. The definition reads the answer as the verb phrase 'lay over', not the noun for a stopover.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something over a surface is to spread it on top, to cover it.

clue.text: 19 down 23 7, 1998, Conservative, getting right into his painting, framing female one

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
the painting surrounds the next piece as a frame surrounds a picture

parts.note: an oil is a painting done in oils
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A 1998 prizewinner and Tory takes a stand on his own canvas with a woman in frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 down 23 7 is TURNER PRIZE WINNER, from those three answers. 'getting' is only a link before 'into'.
explanation.definitionFit: This artist, famous for paintings using elephant dung, won the Turner Prize in 1998.

clue.text: Escape trouble with wild bear captured by a couple of cards

indicators.note: being captured by something is being held inside it

parts.note: J for jack and K for king are two playing cards
to ail is to trouble

indicators.note: wild means the letters of bear run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting free means facing a fierce bear while trapped between two cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges the letters of bear to BREA; 'captured by' puts the trouble-plus-bear run between the two card letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakout from prison is an escape.

clue.text: Women's secret hero

parts.note: W is short for women
inner can mean private or hidden, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A ladies' magazine reveals a hidden champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who triumphs is celebrated as a champion or hero of the day.

clue.text: Ludicrously, this dire man 19 down 23 7, 1995

indicators.note: something done ludicrously is done absurdly, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A provocative artist is mocked as a dreadful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ludicrously' rearranges THIS DIRE MAN. 19 down 23 7 is TURNER PRIZE WINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: This artist, known for a shark in formaldehyde, won the Turner Prize in 1995.

clue.text: Interpretation of actions by intransigence

indicators.note: an interpretation gives a new rendering of the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reading stubbornness into what someone does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interpretation of' rearranges ACTIONS BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn refusal to compromise is both intransigence and obstinacy.

clue.text: Pronouced fall, as a rule

indicators.note: pronounced (misspelt in the clue) means the word is said aloud and matched by sound

parts.note: rain is a fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A remark that, normally, something drops.
explanation.walkthrough: RAIN said out loud matches the answer. The clue as published misspells 'pronounced'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of power is their rule over a kingdom.

clue.text: Actor, 19 down 23 7, 1999

definitions.meaning: a Hollywood film star of The Great Escape and Bullitt
a British artist and film-maker of the same name won the Turner Prize in 1999

explanation.definitionFit: Two men share this name: the American screen star and the British artist who later directed 12 Years a Slave.

clue.text: Home base hides relative, so unseen

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: one word conceals the other inside it

parts.note: base means low or vile
sib is short for sibling, a relative

explanation.surface: Somebody's degraded house is concealing a family member out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' signals the container; 'so' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be seen is invisible.

clue.text: See 11
In possession of a licence, though provisional

definitions.meaning: certified to practise, such as a licensed doctor or driver

explanation.surface: Someone holds a permit, although it is only temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both officially certified and restricted with conditions, as in qualified support.

clue.text: Artist with red line and colour study, becoming 19 down 23 7, 1993

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
Che Guevara is the archetypal red, a revolutionary communist
white is a colour
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: An artist with a revolutionary streak and a pale palette goes on to win a 1993 award.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 down 23 7 is TURNER PRIZE WINNER; 'becoming' joins wordplay to definition. To read a subject is British for studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: This sculptor, who cast the inside of a whole house in concrete, won the Turner Prize in 1993.

clue.text: The 19th card Posh slipped into socks

parts.note: a club is a playing card of that suit

indicators.note: one piece is slipped inside the other

parts.note: hose are socks or stockings
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A smart card ends up stuffed inside someone's socks.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British usage. The '19th hole' is golfers' slang for the bar after the eighteen holes of a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers call the clubhouse bar the nineteenth hole, where the round ends with a drink.

clue.text: Scorer's name announced

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so this reads as scorer is

indicators.note: announced means the word is said aloud and matched by sound

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A goalscorer's name is read out over the tannoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' looks like a goalscorer but is a composer, one who writes scores; HANDLE said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer of Messiah wrote musical scores, so he is a scorer.

clue.text: Perfect going topless, as anarchic

indicators.note: losing the top means the first letter goes, here in a down entry

parts.note: perfect means without a flaw

explanation.surface: Daringly removing one's top is described as perfect and unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the F from FLAWLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A society without law has no order, which is anarchy.

clue.text: Driver finds Rolf's head in Australian food

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the food word

parts.note: tucker is Australian slang for food

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A motorist finds an entertainer's head in his dinner Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the head of Rolf, goes inside TUCKER; Rolf Harris was an Australian entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorry driver is called this in American and Australian usage.

clue.text: One swirling, perhaps — as would be his brush?

definitions.text: One swirling, perhaps — as would be his brush?

parts.words: One swirling, perhaps — as would be his brush?
parts.note: someone who spins or rotates, and also the English painter of swirling storms and seas, whose brush would turn as he painted

explanation.definitionFit: A person who rotates is literally one who turns, and the painter of swirling skies bears that name.

clue.text: Again deal with withdrawal

definitions.meaning: to handle or process a second time, treat again
a pulling back, as of an army

explanation.definitionFit: Split as re-treat it means handle again; as one word it is a military pullback or a quiet refuge.

clue.text: Blank charter on Gibraltar holds up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the words hold the run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A Gibraltar charter is said to delay something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' finds ERONGI across 'charter on Gibraltar'; 'up' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To blank someone is to cut them dead, deliberately taking no notice.

clue.text: New pair go off to win election

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh couple sets off to campaign for office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges NEW PAIR GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning an election means taking control of government, gaining power.

clue.text: Noses by the ear, all eyes on this?

indicators.note: judging by the ear means the word is heard and matched by sound

parts.note: to nose is to pry, so noses means pries

explanation.surface: Someone is snooping by listening, while everyone watches.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIES said out loud gives the answer. The definition plays on the phrase 'keep your eyes on the prize'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying about keeping eyes on a goal makes the reward the thing everyone watches.

clue.text: See 8
River runs back, almost reaching top of estuary

parts.note: R is short for runs in cricket

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: hind means back, as in hind legs

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A river flows back, nearly getting to the head of its estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal but is HIND, which 'almost' cuts to HIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This major European river flows from the Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: See 5
Following river to channel, I have to find high position

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a cut is a channel such as a canal
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Following a river down to the sea leads someone to a lofty place.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior management post is an executive role, a high position in a company.

clue.text: Straight, with no beginning? Quite the opposite!

definitions.text: Straight, with no beginning? Quite the opposite!

parts.words: Straight, with no beginning? Quite the opposite!
parts.note: a straight line has no beginning, and the opposite of having no beginning is having no end

explanation.definitionFit: A line with no end goes on forever, which is what the word means.

clue.text: Abandon wasteland

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to forsake; as a noun it is a dry barren region such as the Sahara.
